codeSnippets.description: StorageService coordinating dual persistence to OPFS and IndexedDB with quota detection and rollback

patterns.codeStructure: src/services/storage/types.ts (StorageAdapter interface) -> src/services/storage/indexeddb-adapter.ts & opfs-adapter.ts (Implementations) -> src/services/storage/quota.ts (Quota classification) -> src/services/storage/services.ts (StorageService orchestrator)
considerations: OPFS is supported in modern browsers (Chrome, Safari 15.2+, Firefox 111+); fallback strategy needed for legacy environments.
Object URLs created from OPFS files must be revoked when no longer needed to prevent memory leaks.
IndexedDB database names are partitioned by project ID to allow clean atomic project deletion.
keyImplementationPoints: Implement generic StorageAdapter<T> interface defining get, set, remove, list, and clear methods.
Store binary files directly in OPFS via FileSystemDirectoryHandle with streaming writers.
Store asset metadata (dimensions, size, mime type, thumbnail) in IndexedDB for fast indexing.
Perform atomic compensation/rollback if saving to one adapter fails.
Provide quota detection via StorageQuotaExceededError with byte requirements.
patterns.overview: A dual-layer client persistence architecture that offloads large binary assets (blobs, images, audio, video) to the Origin Private File System (OPFS) while maintaining queryable structured metadata and project manifests in IndexedDB.
patterns.purpose: Prevents IndexedDB memory bloat and structured serialization bottlenecks during heavy media operations while maintaining fast metadata queries and transactional integrity.
patterns.summary: A hybrid client persistence pattern combining IndexedDB for structured JSON metadata queries and OPFS for zero-overhead binary media blobs with quota guards and rollback.
patterns.title: Hybrid Client Storage (IndexedDB Metadata + OPFS Binary Assets)

codeSnippets.description: Branded MediaTime type with integer ticks arithmetic and second conversions

patterns.codeStructure: src/lib/media-time.ts (Branded MediaTime type, constructor, arithmetic, conversions) -> src/lib/math.ts (Fractional frame math) -> src/editor/editor-store.ts (Timeline state consumption)
considerations: Ensure all arithmetic is performed with integer ticks before converting to seconds for UI display.
Serializing to JSON should convert MediaTime to integer ticks or seconds based on contract.
keyImplementationPoints: Use TypeScript branded type (number & { [MediaTimeBrand]?: never }) to prevent raw number assignment bugs.
Define TICKS_PER_SECOND = 120,000 as a common multiple for 24, 25, 30, 48, and 60 FPS.
Enforce integer assertions at constructor boundaries.
Implement pure integer arithmetic functions (addMediaTime, subtractMediaTime, roundMediaTime).
patterns.overview: A pure TypeScript rational time representation using branded integer ticks to eliminate floating-point drift and rounding errors across audio/video timeline calculations.
patterns.purpose: Eliminates frame drift, sub-pixel rendering misalignment, and precision loss caused by IEEE 754 floating-point arithmetic when positioning clips and playheads across varied frame rates.
patterns.summary: Integer-ticks-based media time representation using TypeScript branded types to eliminate floating-point inaccuracies in audio/video timeline editing.
patterns.title: High-Precision Rational Media Time & Ticks Arithmetic

codeSnippets.description: Zustand store handling project loading, media URL hydration, and timeline state

patterns.codeStructure: src/editor/editor-store.ts (Zustand state store and actions) -> src/editor/use-editor.ts (Hook interface) -> src/pages/Editor/* (UI canvas and timeline views)
considerations: Revoke existing object URLs when loading a different project or deleting elements.
Keep scene hierarchy modifications immutable for predictable rendering.
keyImplementationPoints: Separate persistent project hierarchy from transient runtime UI state (mediaUrls, isPlaying).
Asynchronously hydrate media asset IDs into active memory Object URLs on project load.
Provide granular actions for element additions, deletions, track muting, and selection.
Centralize timeline view state (zoomLevel, scrollLeft, playheadTime).
patterns.overview: A centralized Zustand store managing multi-track scene hierarchies, multi-element selection, playback state, and dynamic asset URL hydration.
patterns.purpose: Coordinates complex UI interactions across multi-track timeline canvases while keeping UI state updates decoupled from async persistence.
patterns.summary: Hierarchical Zustand-based state store for multi-track non-linear media editing with asynchronous blob hydration, multi-selection, and debounced persistence.
patterns.title: Non-Linear Timeline & Multi-Track Editor State Management

codeSnippets.description: React Query polling pattern with conditional refetch interval and mutation trigger

patterns.codeStructure: src/services/generate.ts (API endpoints) -> src/services/hooks/useGenerate.tsx (TanStack Query hooks & toast orchestration)
considerations: Clear promptId on network errors or component unmounting.
Handle browser tab backgrounding throttling polling intervals gracefully.
keyImplementationPoints: Use useMutation for initiating multipart async jobs and useQuery for polling job status.
Conditionally terminate refetchInterval when job status reaches terminal states.
Expose an imperative jumpTo100 API from toast progress component via ref callback.
Trigger automatic file download upon successful job completion using blob URLs.
patterns.overview: A two-phase async workflow coordinating multipart job submission via TanStack Query mutation with polling query status checks, interactive progress toast, and automatic file download.
patterns.purpose: Manages long-running server-side generation jobs with smooth progress feedback, automatic polling termination, error recovery, and automated download triggers.
patterns.summary: An async orchestration pattern combining TanStack Query mutations and polling queries with interactive toast progress and automated artifact downloading.
patterns.title: Async Multi-Stage Job Polling & UI Progress Orchestration
